the decision boundaries of all investigated networks are very similar, and that ImageNet validation set is dominated by "trivial" or "impossible" examples, and that humans are good at predicting the "difficulty" of examples for CNNs.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that the ImageNet dataset has an inbuilt dichotomous difficulty distribution, which makes it very hard for models to learn anything beyond trivial or impossible images.

(i.) CNNs are highly similar in their inductive biases (ii.) the ImageNet validation dataset suffers from DDD (iii.) humans are surprisingly accurate at predicting which data is "trivial" or "impossible" (iv.) removing the DDD allows us to see differences between models.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the ImageNet dataset, and perhaps many others, is not suitable to investigate the differences between models' decision boundaries, because it is dominated by "impossible" or "trivial" data points.
